deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous page. Read λ as log, so e^{sλ(x)} = x^s. Hilbert has the double series g(z,z'') = Σ_{μ≥0, ν∈Z} [(μz+ν)(μz''+ν)]^{-s}, with Im z>0 and Im z''<0. It satisfies g(z+1,z''+1)=g(z,z'') and an automorphy relation under (z,z'')→(−1/z,−1/z''). Putting z=ξ+iη, z''=ξ−iη gives Σ ψ^{-s} with ψ=|μz+ν|^2. This is the non-holomorphic Eisenstein series / Epstein zeta function of a positive binary form. The first line of this page finishes that sentence: '…the function Σ 1/ψ^s of Dirichlet, Kronecker, Weber.'

(1) Change of variables. Hilbert writes the variables as z, z'; they are the z, z'' of the previous page. Set u=z+z'' and v=zz''.
- Then (μz+ν)(μz''+ν) = vμ² + uμν + ν².
- Swapping the summation letters gives Hilbert's later form μ² + uμν + vν². The sum is symmetric under this swap, so g is a function of (u,v).
- Translation (z,z'')→(z+1,z''+1) induces u→u+2, v→v+u+1.
- Inversion (z,z'')→(−1/z,−1/z'') induces u→−u/v, v→1/v.
- In homogeneous coordinates (w:u:v), with w=1, both maps are linear ternary substitutions: (w,u,v)→(w, u+2w, v+u+w) and (w,u,v)→(v,−u,w).
- Both preserve the quadratic form u²−4wv. This is the discriminant (z−z'')². Hence the conic u²−4wv=0 is invariant: the 'gewisser Kegelschnitt'.
- [Mine] This is the homomorphism SL2(Z)→SO(2,1)(Z) given by the symmetric square. Positive definite forms (4v−u²>0) form the interior of the conic, i.e. the Klein model of the hyperbolic plane.

(2) Remark on further series that might be useful for ζ-function studies: f(z,t,q) = Σ_{μ≥0, ν∈Z} q^ν (t+μz+ν)^{-s}.
- This is a two-dimensional Lerch/Hurwitz-type series with a character q^ν.
- [Mine] Functional equations: f(z,t+1,q) = q^{-1} f(z,t,q). Also t→t+z shifts μ by one, so f(z,t,q) − f(z,t+z,q) = Σ_ν q^ν (t+ν)^{-s}, the Lerch zeta function.

(3) Congruence subgroup (p). Use the earlier Eisenstein-type series ψ, φ to build the simplest functions belonging to the congruence group mod p. Do this by substituting something like τ = (·)/p and taking combinations with a character.
- One must show the resulting series does not vanish at the cusp z=i∞, 'by Cauchy's theorem'.
- Hilbert notes this is equivalent to Dirichlet's theorem Σ_{k=1}^{p−1} α^{ind k}/k^{s−1} ≠ 0. Here α is a root of unity of order dividing p−1 and ind is the index (discrete log) to a primitive root, so α^{ind k} = χ(k) is a Dirichlet character mod p.
- [Mine] The constant term of the twisted Eisenstein series of weight s at ∞ is a multiple of L(s−1,χ), truncated to k<p. Hence 'non-vanishing at i∞' ⇔ L(s−1,χ) ≠ 0.
- The bracket labels this the link between Hurwitz's theory of modular functions and Dirichlet series.

(4) Return to Σ (μ²+uμν+vν²)^{-s} as a function of (u,v).
- It is invariant under the ternary linear substitutions preserving 4v−u².
- This motivates the next page: Σ ψ^{-s} for an n-ary form ψ = Σ u_ik v_i v_k, viewed as a function of its coefficients. That is an Epstein zeta function on the cone of positive forms, with invariance group GL_n(Z) acting on the coefficients.
errors: Invariance is only up to an automorphy factor. Under u→−u/v, v→1/v one gets G(−u/v,1/v) = v^s G(u,v); 'ungeändert' holds only for the homogeneous version in (w,u,v), with degree −s.

'Bei allen denen, welche die Form 4v−u² ungeändert lassen' is overstated. Only the integral substitutions induced by GL2(Z) on (μ,ν) are meant. They must also map the cone of positive forms to itself: −identity preserves the form but not the sum. Not every real or integral orthogonal transformation qualifies.

The 'Dirichlet theorem' reduction is a reformulation, not a proof: non-vanishing at i∞ is equivalent to L(s−1,χ)≠0. For s−1>1 this follows trivially from the Euler product. The real content is s−1=1, where the Eisenstein series converges only conditionally and Hecke's trick is needed. 'Anwendung des Cauchyschen Satzes' is not carried out.
Minor: 'ungeändert bleiben' should agree with the singular subject 'Funktion' (bleibt). Hilbert writes the variables as z, z' although on the previous page they are z, z''.

results.what: Non-holomorphic Eisenstein series Σ|μz+ν|^{-2s} rewritten as a function of the symmetric functions u=z+z'', v=zz''. The modular group then acts by ternary linear substitutions preserving the conic u²−4wv.
results.modern_name: Real-analytic Eisenstein series / Epstein zeta; SL2 ≅ SO(2,1) via symmetric square; Klein model of hyperbolic plane as space of positive binary forms
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet, Kronecker (limit formula, 1880s), Weber (Elliptische Functionen 1891); conic model: Klein, Poincaré (1881), Fricke–Klein

results.what: Double series f(z,t,q)=Σ q^ν (t+μz+ν)^{-s}, μ≥0, proposed for ζ-function studies
results.modern_name: Twisted Barnes double zeta / Lerch-type double series (Shintani-type zeta)

results.what: Non-vanishing at the cusp of Eisenstein series with character for Γ(p) identified with non-vanishing of Dirichlet L-values Σ χ(k) k^{1−s}
results.modern_name: Constant term of Eisenstein series with Nebentypus ∝ L(s−1,χ); modular-forms viewpoint on L(1,χ)≠0

deep.surprise_reason: The binary material and the conic/ternary viewpoint are classical (Kronecker, Weber, Klein, Poincaré). Notable but speculative are the twisted double series and the remark linking the cusp behaviour of congruence-group Eisenstein series to Dirichlet's L(χ)≠0. Together with the next page's coefficient-space Epstein zeta, these anticipate later lines (Hecke, Epstein, Siegel/Koecher). They are research sketches without proofs, so the surprise is modest.
